tooling_gaps: ExportAllCollisions batch command (src/JUS.CLI/JUS/CombatCommands.cs) has never been run against the full character .bin directory -- closes the 4/74 -> 74/74 collision-data coverage gap flagged by both B9's miner and its verify lens; would let collision-data's PLAUSIBLE distributional claims (collisionType->hitTier skew, projectileId sentinel value) be re-tested at full-roster scale and likely promoted toward CONFIRMED_STATIC.

query.py search-imm only indexes load/store immediate *offsets*; it cannot find data-processing immediate *operands* (mov/cmp/tst/and #imm). Independently flagged by movement round1 (no way to search for 'cmp r,#0x22' walk-speed thresholds) and physics-writers round1 (no way to find the 0xC0 launched-state writer). Blocks B13's hasSpecialFlag/hitProperties bit-consumer search and any future flag-gated completeness target from being ROM-wide-searchable without manual disasm reading.

No register-provenance-aware search exists (only immediate-offset text matching) -- independently flagged as the single biggest false-positive source by hitstun-timers (a 172-byte settings object and an entity+0xa4 combo-record both coincidentally overlap +0x98-0xba), physics-writers (ov7's folded +0x100 base aliasing +0x68/+0x6a/+0x6c), and weight-hunt. A tool that tags a register as 'provably descended from anchor X' via forward call-graph walk, rather than matching a bare immediate byte, would directly serve B10 and eliminate most of this campaign's aliasing false-positives.

jpower-indirect's div-by-5 callsite sweep (xrefs-to 0x0200D12C, 324 sites) used a fixed ARM-only -8-byte lookback for the divisor-setting instruction and explicitly could not check Thumb-mode call sites. A lookback that walks backward through the actual instruction stream respecting ARM/Thumb mode (rather than a fixed byte offset) would let that sweep be re-run with confidence it isn't missing the real formula's ÷5 call site.

weight-hunt's arm9_tables.json scanner artifact found ~7 candidate ~74-entry data tables and several 70-78-entry code-pointer vtables by ROM FILE OFFSET, but round1 never translated those file offsets to RAM addresses, so none could be run through xrefs-to/callers. A small offset-translation helper reusing rom_loader.py's already-built region map would unlock that whole candidate list for a cheap follow-up pass.
